articles.headline: Bowie at 68%, Adam at 32%: the Week 11 model, annotated
body: Before the narrative, the numbers. Week 11's featured game is Bowie (7-3, 159.0 points per game) against Adam (5-5, 130.2), and Bowie already holds the season series 1-0 (a sample of one). The stakes are lopsided: Bowie sits at 100% playoff odds and Adam at 37%, with the simulations moving Adam to 54% with a win and 28% with a loss. The model makes Bowie the favorite at 68% to Adam's 32%. Variance note: Adam swings by 35.7 points a week, Bowie by 19.9. “1-0. That's not trash talk, that's a citation,” said Bowie. Adam, uncited: “I'd answer Bowie, but I try not to reward noise.”

Tom (7-3, 182.1) meets Cian (1-9, 113.2); they have not played each other this season, so the head-to-head column is blank. Playoff odds are 100% and 0% either way, and Tom is the favorite at 85% to 15%. Tom's standard deviation is 38.5 against Cian's 29.8 (the wider distribution belongs to the better team). “I'm going to play the spoiler, the villain, and the fan who refuses to leave early,” Cian said, confidence interval unknown.

Steven (7-3, 162.2) leads Nick (2-8, 114.8) 1-0 on the season, and the model concurs at 82% to 18%. The spreads are nearly identical (25.0 for Steven, 26.4 for Nick). “0-1. I've got a lot of notes on how Steven did it, and I'm going to use every one,” Nick said.
Michael (7-3, 163.7) is 1-0 against Colin (5-5, 138.5) and favored 70% to 30%. “Michael has me 0-1 this year. A person can only be owned for so long,” said Colin, with no controls.

Jimmy (7-3, 150.5) leads Patrick (2-8, 134.4) 1-0. Jimmy is at 100% playoff odds and Patrick at 0%, so the leverage is cosmetic, and the model has Jimmy at 61% to 39% (the closest line on the slate). “I've beaten Patrick this year and I plan on doing it again, so whatever Patrick is working on, work on it harder,” Jimmy said, n = 1.
Yes, but (and the confidence interval is wide): Tom's schedule has been soft.
The model will be revised as the season is.

articles.headline: Week 11 variance report: Tom 173.62, Cian 89.68
body: Leadership update. The Week 11 results are in, and the headline item is a material variance: Tom delivered 173.62 against Cian's 89.68, an 83.94-point blowout. One compliance item: Tom owes 1 shotgun for starting Brock Bowers (TE). The 173.62 was the top performance of Week 11, measured against a league benchmark of 133.12, with Jahmyr Gibbs (RB) contributing 26.30 points. Cian, who has not been physically seen since the draft, closes the period at 1-10 and 10th.
“We exceeded target by 83.94 points and I see no need for a retrospective,” Tom said. “I would describe the week as a learning experience, and 89.68 as the tuition,” Cian added.

Adam 136.22, Bowie 130.86: a 5.36-point escape, and a variance to forecast, since the pre-week rankings had Bowie 4th and Adam 7th. Adam owes 1 shotgun for starting Rachaad White (RB). Top individual contributor: Emmett Johnson (RB), 23.30 points, 17% of Adam's total. “A 5.36-point margin is what we call lean operations,” Adam noted.

Steven outperformed Nick, 159.89 to 111.88, a 48.01-point blowout. Dak Prescott (QB) contributed 35.90 points, 22% of the total. That is 6 consecutive wins for Steven, now 8-3 and 3rd. Resourcing note for Nick: 19.60 points went unallocated on the bench, 8.50 points of it from Germie Bernard (WR).

Jimmy closed out Patrick, 128.95 to 113.33, a margin of 15.62. Patrick left 47.06 points on the bench, including 21.10 points from Ted Hurst III (WR), and is 2-9 and 8th with 3 straight losses. This is a leadership opportunity.
Michael over Colin, 149.65 to 137.16, a 12.49-point result. Colin owes 1 shotgun for starting J.K. Dobbins (RB), who returned 0 points. Michael has 5 straight wins and sits 2nd at 8-3.
Standings realignment: Adam moves into the top six, and Colin moves out. Tom remains 1st at 8-3.
End of digest. Synergies to follow.

articles.headline: Week 11 ledger lists 3 shotguns across 3 owners
body: In brief: the league ledger recorded 3 shotguns for Week 11, owed by 3 owners at 1 shotgun apiece.

Adam owed 1 shotgun for starting Rachaad White (RB), who scored 0 points, according to the box score. Colin owed 1 shotgun for J.K. Dobbins (RB), who also scored 0 points. Tom owed 1 shotgun for Brock Bowers (TE), listed at 0 points. The ledger filed all 3 entries under the same heading: zero points from a starter.
Cian was not listed for Week 11 but remained the season leader, with 10 shotguns through Week 11, the ledger showed.
“The ledger says 1 shotgun, and I do not dispute the ledger,” Adam said in a statement. “Rachaad White was in my lineup. That part was my decision.”
No other owner was listed for the week. The figures stand.
Developing.

articles.headline: Michael Wins a Fifth Straight, and the Ledger Declines to Applaud
body: From the beat desk: Michael beat Colin 149.65 to 137.16 in Week 11, a 12.49-point win. Credit is noted. It is not framed.

The ledger. Scoring rank: 3 of 10, against a league average of 133.12. Bench points left: 2.20, which is tidy work for an owner who answers lineup questions from a work bathroom. Record: 8-3. Rank: 2. Streak: W5. Receipts available on request.

Five straight wins is the kind of run an owner calls momentum and an auditor calls a schedule. The playoff odds read 100%, so nothing about the next few weeks needs Michael's judgment, which is the safest place for it.
The star of the week was Travis Kelce (TE), who put up 28.40 points. Michael's contribution was leaving Kelce in the lineup. That is a low bar, and the owner cleared it.
Second place with a five-game streak is a fine position. It is also a position the roster built while the owner was busy treating the waiver wire like a sportsbook.
The ledger will be updated next week, whether or not the owner is.

articles.headline: Patrick Leaves 29.36 Points on the Bench and Still Has a Trade to Defend
body: Stop the presses: Patrick lost to Jimmy 128.95 to 113.33 in Week 11, and the margin was 15.62 points. Score 113.33 ranked 8 of 10 in a week that averaged 133.12.

Now read the lineup page. Patrick left 29.36 points on the bench, nearly double the margin of defeat. Jack Bech (WR) alone put up 20.80 points over there. The best lineup was worth 142.69. That is not bad luck. That is a filing error.

The record is 2-9, rank 8, streak L3. Patrick has also traded Rashee Rice (WR) to Colin for a 2027 round 2 pick, a deal still pending, and added Harrison Wallace III (WR) on a $20 bid, one of 3 adds this week. Patrick has never met a trade he didn't want to make, and then regret. Write that down. The playoff odds, meanwhile, are gone.
Busy hands, empty bench logic. Patrick, “Pat” to the group chat, moved plenty of players this week and somehow not the right ones.
Thirty. (That is how we used to end a story.)

articles.headline: Jimmy Wins at 8-3 While the Expected Record Says 6-5
body: Pull up a chair, folks. Jimmy beat Patrick 128.95 to 113.33 in Week 11, and the owner is going to take a bow. Let us ask a few questions first.

Question one: how good was a score that ranked 7 of 10? 6 teams outscored Jimmy this week, and the win still counted, because the schedule handed over Patrick. Question two: why does an 8-3 record sit beside an expected record of 6-5? Luck, and plenty of it. Bench points left were 10.45, so the lineup was not even tidy.

Question three: does anyone think the 100% playoff odds came from skill alone? Rank 4 says the owner is doing fine, and fine is the word. The win ends a two-game slide and starts a streak of W1. I've seen this movie, and the sequel is usually a loss.
Jimmy opens a booster pack every time his team scores. A 128.95 week means a pack got opened, and I hope it held something better than the lineup did.
That's the beat, and I'm stuck with it.

articles.headline: Bowie Loses by 5.36 and Starts Makai Lemon for 0.80 Points
body: There is a particular sadness to this beat: Bowie lost to Adam 136.22 to 130.86 in Week 11, a 5.36-point miss, and the loss has a clear author.
Notes. Score rank 6 of 10 against a league average of 133.12. Bench points left: 7.50, which is more than enough to cover the gap's worth of regret. Record 7-4, rank 5, streak L1.
Note one: Anthony Richardson Sr. (QB) arrived on a $50 bid, one of 2 adds, and has returned 0 points since. Fifty dollars buys a lot of nothing.
Note two: Makai Lemon (WR) started and returned 0.80 points. In a game decided by 5.36, a starter that quiet is a decision, and the decision was Bowie's.
Note three: the playoff odds still read 99%, so the season survives the lineup. Ashton Jeanty (RB) scored 25.40 points, which is what made the game close enough to hurt.
Bowie treats every loss like an Eagles playoff exit. I have been asked to be fair. I am trying. This one was a regular-season Week 11 loss at 99%, and the owner can calm down.
And so the season goes on, as seasons do.

articles.headline: Tom Posts the Week's Best Score, 173.62, and Somehow Still Gets Doubted
body: UPDATE: Tom beat Cian 173.62 to 89.68 in Week 11, an 83.94-point blowout. (More as it develops.)
The facts, reluctantly. Tom left 4.50 points on the bench, so even the clean sheet has a smudge. The league average was 133.12, and Tom cleared it by a distance that suggests the roster did the work.

Tom also picked up 1 shotgun, for starting Brock Bowers (TE). Credit the owner for finding a way to win big and earn a penalty in the same Sunday. The 173.62 was the best score in the league, 1 of 10, which the roster would like noted.
The record is 8-3, rank 1, streak W2, with playoff odds of 100%. Tom leads the league, and the owner will explain this as vision.
A word on perspective: Tom won a title and his dad asked how the fish were. A week like this one should help, though the beat wouldn't count on it.
Refresh for more disappointment.

articles.headline: Adam Wins 136.22-130.86 and Still Leaves 22.68 Points on the Bench
body: Look, I want to be positive. Adam beat Bowie, 136.22 to 130.86, a 5.36-point margin that Nice Tates will cheerfully file under progress. The record is now 6-5, sixth place, with a streak of W1.

Three questions, then. Why did the lineup page cost Adam 1 shotgun for starting Rachaad White (RB)? Why did the bench hold 22.68 points when the best possible lineup was worth 158.90? And why did Joe Burrow (QB) get the start, with 19.90 points, while Fernando Mendoza (QB) sat on the bench with 22.88?

The scoring rank was 5 of 10, against a league average of 133.12. Playoff odds sit at 59%, which is a number built on a win, not on lineup work. Efficiency was 79%, 10th in the league, and the season total left on the bench is 378.10 points.
To be fair, and I am trying to be fair: Adam says nothing in the group chat for weeks, then makes a trade nobody understands. The lineup page, it turns out, gets the same treatment.
I will remain optimistic, professionally.

articles.headline: Steven Wins by 48.01 and Takes the Credit
body: Exclusive: Ja’Mario Kart beat Nick, 159.89 to 111.88, a 48.01-point blowout, and the owner is expected to claim all of it.

Grade for Steven's week: C+. A win this size earns a better mark from most desks, but 26.90 points stayed on the bench, against a best possible lineup of 186.79. Justice Hill (RB) alone put up 16.60 points there. The scoring rank was 2 of 10, with the league average at 133.12.
That is six straight wins, and the record is 8-3, third place. Playoff odds stand at 100%. Draw your own conclusions; I drew mine.
Dak Prescott (QB) did the heavy lifting with 35.90 points. Credit to the quarterback. The owner merely pressed save, probably at 4 a.m. with Daft Punk on, which is when Steven sets the lineup.
The facts are in: this team wins in spite of the lineup page, not because of it. A source of income nobody in the league can explain would at least buy a better bench read.
You read it here first, unfortunately.

articles.headline: Cian Falls 83.94 Behind, and the Lineup Page Is a Crime Scene
body: Dateline: the group chat. Tank for Tank lost to Tom, 173.62 to 89.68, a blowout of 83.94 points, and the only person in the building who could have prevented it is the owner.

Three questions. At what point does a streak become a plan? That is ten straight losses and a record of 1-10, tenth place. Why did Kyle Monangai (RB) start and score 1.80 points while Evan Engram (TE) sat on the bench with 17.40? And what, exactly, was the thinking behind Quentin Johnston (WR), who returned 1.50 points?
Bench points left: 19.20. The best available lineup was worth 108.88, which would still have lost, but at least it would have been a loss with dignity.
The 89.68 was the lowest score of the week, 10 of 10, against a league average of 133.12. I have seen the lineup. I am not able to say more.
Cian sets the lineup from a different time zone every week, which explains the timing, if not the result. Nobody has been told which time zone is responsible.
More from the field as the situation deteriorates.

articles.headline: Nick Draws an F, and the Bench Holds the Evidence
body: Exhibit A is the box score. First-Down Syndrome lost to Steven, 159.89 to 111.88, by 48.01, and the court gives Nick an F for the week.

Exhibit B is the bench. Nick left 19.20 points there, and the best possible lineup was worth 131.08. Germie Bernard (WR) scored 8.50 points in the seat reserved for spectators. The scoring rank was 9 of 10, with the league average at 133.12.
Exhibit C is the standings. At 2-9, ninth place, with a streak of L2, Nick is out of the playoff race. Objection overruled.

The defense will point to Michael Mayer (TE), who started and returned 1.65 points. The court notes that the person who started him is also the owner. Nick finished below the league median in 10 of 11 weeks, and the evidence speaks for itself, and it is loud.
The profile fits the record: Nick makes the trade everyone in the group chat begged him not to make, and drops a player the week before he goes off. A pattern is a pattern.
The court is adjourned. The owner is not acquitted.

articles.headline: Colin Falls Short by 12.49 and Still Has a Shotgun to Explain
body: The data, such as it is: Sauvignon Charbonnet lost to Michael, 149.65 to 137.16, a 12.49-point gap. The week's scoring rank was 4 of 10, against a league average of 133.12. The record is 5-6, seventh place, streak L1. Bench points left: 5.70.

Colin also took 1 shotgun for starting J.K. Dobbins (RB). Run the numbers and weep. Newest addition to the roster is Rashee Rice (WR), from Patrick, for a 2027 round 2 pick. The deal is still pending, so judgment is reserved. (Methodology: watching.)

In fairness, a 137.16 beats the average and still lost. The schedule was unkind this week, and Colin will say so. Variance is not an alibi, but it is a decent footnote. Playoff odds are 41%, which is the kind of number that invites optimism and punishes it.
Colin, “Colon Burns” to the group chat, cites the Rule of 5 for every decision, including trades. The Rule of 5 did not start Dobbins. The owner did.
Sample size noted. Sympathy not included.

articles.headline: Patrick Sells Rashee Rice (WR) to Colin for a 2027 Round 2 Pick
body: Consider, if you will, the week that was. In Week 11 Patrick handed Rashee Rice (WR) to Colin and took back a 2027 round 2 pick, a swap with all the drama of two neighbors trading tools over a fence.

Each side got what it came for. Patrick receives a 2027 round 2 pick; Colin receives Rashee Rice (WR). The old ballparks had their sellers of tomorrow and their buyers of today, and which is which in this deal depends entirely on the weather ahead.

There is no grade to hand out yet. Rice has scored 0.0 points for Colin since the deal, and the weeks since stand at 0, so the books are closed to opinion. Patrick, who has never met a trade he didn't want to make, and then regret, now stands at 7 trades and 30 claims. Colin stands at 3 trades and 13 claims. A little perspective never hurt a standings page.
So we wait, the way one waits in a barbershop for a name to be called. Consider it considered.

articles.headline: Bowie Pays $50 for Anthony Richardson Sr. (QB), and the Radar Shows 0.0
body: Forecast models show a lively system this week. The big front came from Bowie, who put down $50 for Anthony Richardson Sr. (QB), the top bid of Week 11.
Readings since the claim: 0.0 points. That is a flat barometer for a $50 purchase, though the instruments have only just been switched on.

Elsewhere on the map, Patrick was busy. Harrison Wallace III (WR) came in at $20, Matt Hibner (TE) at $3 and Jack Endries (TE) at $2, three smaller disturbances with the risk spread around. Bowie also picked up Dohnte Meyers (WR) on the side.

And out at the edge of the radar, a light drizzle: Jimmy added Will Shipley (RB) for $1. It barely registers on the gauge, but a $1 shower has the advantage of not ruining anybody's weekend. Expect a scattering of drama.
Add it up and the week logged 6 adds, with the heaviest pressure parked over Bowie, a steady band over Patrick and a single passing cloud over Jimmy.
That's the outlook. Do dress in layers.
